correctness.rationale: All three rows are linearly independent unit normals. Orthogonal-projector trace identity gives tr(M^T M)=Q+p; exterior-square Hodge identity gives the product of the nonzero squared singular values p, hence the stated radical formula. Gram positive definiteness gives 0<=Q<1 and feasibility bounds on p. The larger root has derivative (L-1)/sqrt((Q+p)^2-4p)<0 on feasible interiors, with continuous endpoint treatment. Therefore maximizing adjacent-correlation product exactly minimizes Euclidean sweep norm. The sweep trace and second elementary symmetric polynomial are order-independent, giving common eigenvalues. Uniform Q/2< L <=Q yields ratio \(<\sqrt2\); a nonsingular two-leaf star realizes the supremum in the limit. Python standard-library exact rational checks confirm finite identities; the analytic proof covers all real full-rank triples.

value.rationale: The smallest genuinely ordering-sensitive full-rank cyclic Kaczmarz instance admits a complete computable ordering rule. The contrast between identical eigenvalues and distinct transient singular norms is structurally informative and explains why local consecutive-row orthogonality heuristics need not optimize a first-sweep worst-case objective. The sharp universal sqrt2 penalty and rational witness quantify a nontrivial optimization gap; a larger-dimension or long-horizon theorem is not claimed.
